title: Finite flat descent of regular divisor purity in invertible degree
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite locally free morphism of constant positive rank $d$ with $\ell\nmid d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular effective Cartier divisor and suppose the reduced inverse image $D'=(Y\times_XD)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is also a regular effective Cartier divisor, with inclusion $i'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Effective Cartier means locally cut out by one nonzerodivisor. If
$$A_{D'}\to i'^!A_Y(1)[2]$$
is an isomorphism, then so is
$$A_D\to i^!A_X(1)[2].$$
No assumption that $f$ is generically etale is made.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.3, printed p.246 (the divisor descent assertion itself).

proof.text: Apply the strict-local complement criterion [lem-per-divisor-purity-strict-local-criterion]. To prove purity of $(X,D)$, fix a geometric point $\bar x\to D$, pass to the strict henselization $S=X_{(\bar x)}$, and write $U=S\setminus(D\times_XS)$. The strict-localization Cartesian identification for the closed immersion [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] identifies this divisor with the pullback of $D$ and reduces the desired assertion to $H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)=0$ for $q\ge2$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.2 and Proposition 3.4.3, printed pp.245–246.

proof.text: Put $Y_S=Y\times_XS$. By [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization], $Y_S$ is a finite disjoint union of the strict localizations $Y_{(\bar y_a)}$ at geometric points above $\bar x$. These are regular Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular, lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. The closed-immersion comparison [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] identifies $D'\times_Y Y_{(\bar y_a)}$ with $D'_{(\bar y_a)}$. The closed subsets defined by a Cartier ideal and its radical are equal; thus $V=Y_S\times_SU$ is the disjoint union of the complements of these divisors. The map $g:V\to U$ remains finite locally free of rank $d$: on affine charts its algebra is $B\otimes_R R'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with a finite free rank-$d$ module locally by [lem-pc-flf-properties]; tensoring its local basis gives a rank-$d$ basis after every base change. The rank agreement is also [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso](2). The divisor's reduction is used only to identify its underlying closed set, never to assert it commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.3 p.246; Stacks Tags 03QP (finite strict-local decomposition), 06LJ (Noetherian strict henselization), 06LN (regularity), 02KD (lemma-base-change-finite-locally-free).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-divisor-purity-strict-local-criterion] to the original regular pair $(Y,D')$. The assumed isomorphism implies $H^q(Y_{(\bar y_a)}\setminus D'_{(\bar y_a)},A)=0$ for every $q\ge2$ and every $a$. Step 2 identifies these opens with the components of $V$. Sheaves and injective resolutions on a finite disjoint union are componentwise: sections are the finite product of sections and the category is the product of the component categories. Finite products of vector spaces preserve exact sequences, so taking cohomology of those resolutions gives $H^q(V,A)=\prod_aH^q(Y_{(\bar y_a)}\setminus D'_{(\bar y_a)},A)=0$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.3, strict-henselian reduction, printed p.246.

proof.text: For the finite locally free map $g:V\to U$, the weighted trace theorem [lem-pur-quasifinite-flat-weighted-trace] supplies a trace $\tau:g_*g^*A\to A$ whose composite with the unit $A\to g_*g^*A$ is multiplication by $d$. Since $\ell\nmid d$, multiplication by $d$ is invertible on $A$, so the unit is a split monomorphism. The finite-pushforward derived-sections comparison [lem-trf-derived-sections-finite-pushforward-modules] identifies $R\Gamma(U,g_*A)$ with $R\Gamma(V,A)$; applying cohomology therefore makes $H^q(U,A)\to H^q(V,A)$ injective for every $q$. The vanishing from Step 3 forces $H^q(U,A)=0$ for $q\ge2$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.3 and Lemma 3.4.4, printed p.246.

proof.text: The vanishing in Step 4 holds for every geometric point of $D$. Applying the strict-local complement criterion [lem-per-divisor-purity-strict-local-criterion] gives that the Kummer class map $A_D\to i^!A_X(1)[2]$ is an isomorphism, as required.
